qa.question: Can I use this card's [When Attacking] inherited effect to suspend my Digimon?
qa.answer:
Yes, you can.
This effect doesn't specify a player, so you can specify either player's Digimon as the effect's target.

qa.question: If my opponent's ST18-03 [Falcomon] attacks and this card switches from unsuspended to suspended, can I activate this card's [Opponent's Turn] effect?

If the 3 cards revealed for this card's [On Play] effect include only either 1 card with [Avian] or [Bird] in any of its traits or 1 card with the [Vortex Warriors] or [LIBERATOR] trait, can I just add that 1 card to my hand?
qa.answer:
Yes, you can.
Even if you only reveal one of the applicable cards, you can still add it to your hand.

qa.question: If the 3 cards I reveal from my deck for this card's [On Play] effect include both a card with [Avian] or [Bird] in any of its traits and a card with the [Vortex Warriors] or [LIBERATOR] trait, can I choose to only add one of them to my hand, and place the remaining cards at the bottom of my deck?
qa.answer:
No, you can't.
If you have cards that are targets of this effect, you must add as many cards to your hand as possible.

qa.question: Does this card's [All Turns] effect trigger when this Digimon is suspended by either my effect or my opponent's effect?
qa.answer:
Yes, it triggers.
It triggers regardless of the player that activated the suspending effect.

qa.question: Can I use this card's [Security] effect to play a Tamer card with the [LIBERATOR] trait and a play cost of 4 or less?
qa.answer:
Yes, you can.
You can play it as long as the card has the [LIBERATOR] trait and a play cost of 4 or less.

qa.question: Can I use this card's [Security] effect to play a Digi-Egg card with the [LIBERATOR] trait?
qa.answer:
No, you can't.
You can't play it because Digi-Egg cards don't have play costs.

qa.question: If this card is checked from a security stack, does its [Security] effect activate, then does it battle with the attacking Digimon?
qa.answer: Yes, its [Security] effect activates, then it battles.

qa.question: Can I use this card's [On Play] [When Digivolving] effect to suspend my Digimon?
qa.answer:
Yes, you can.
This effect doesn't specify a player, so you can specify either player's Digimon as the effect's target.

qa.question: If I specify my suspended Digimon for this card's [On Play] [When Digivolving] effect, can I resolve "if this effect suspended your Digimon" effects?
qa.answer:
No, you can't.
Even if you specify an already suspended Digimon as the target for a suspending effect, it isn't considered to be suspended by the effect.

qa.question: If <Raid> switches the target of attack from a player to an opponent's Digimon, does the [Your Turn] effect in this card's inherited effects trigger?
Can the Digimon I specify to suspend be different from the opponent's Digimon that can't unsuspend for this card's [On Play] effect?
Can either my Digimon or my opponent's Digimon be specified for the Digimon that are suspended and unsuspended by this card's [When Digivolving] effect?
qa.answer:
Yes, they can.
This effect doesn't specify a player, so you can specify either player's Digimon as the effect's targets.

qa.question: Does this card's [All Turns] effect trigger when either my Digimon or my opponent's Digimon is unsuspended?
qa.answer:
Yes, it triggers.
It triggers regardless of which player's Digimon is unsuspended.

qa.question: Can I use this card's [Your Turn] effect to switch the target of attack to an opponent's unsuspended Digimon or Digimon with a "can't be attacked" effect?
qa.answer:
Yes, you can.
When using an effect that switches the target of attack after an attack declaration, you can also switch the target of attack to an opponent's unsuspended Digimon or Digimon with a "can't be attacked" effect.

qa.question: Can I process the part of the effect after "then" in this card's [Main] effect even if the "if" condition in the 2nd process isn't met?
qa.answer:
Yes, you can process it.
Even if this card's [Main] effect doesn't suspend your Digimon, 1 Digimon unsuspends.

comprehensive-0223.title: <Blocker>
comprehensive-0223.text:
16-5. <Blocker>
16-5-1. <Blocker> is a keyword effect that applies a rule that allows a Digimon with that effect to block. (For details, refer to 12 "Blocking")
16-5-2. <Blocker> is a persistent effect. (For details, refer to 15-8-2 "Persistent Effects")
16-5-3. Even if 1 Digimon has multiple instances of <Blocker>, the number of blocks that can be performed during the block timing is only 1.

comprehensive-0225.title: <Piercing>
comprehensive-0225.text:
16-7. <Piercing>
16-7-1. <Piercing> is a keyword effect that reads "When this Digimon deletes your opponent's Digimon in battle while attacking, it checks security before the attack ends." (For details, refer to 13 "Security Checks")
16-7-2. <Piercing> is a trigger-type effect that triggers and activates when a Digimon with this effect battles an opponent's Digimon and the opponent's Digimon is deleted in battle. (For details, refer to 15-8-3 "Trigger- Type Effects")
16-7-3. The security check from using <Piercing> is mandatory.
16-7-4. <Piercing> is pending processing that is processed immediately before the transition to the end of attack timing. Therefore, it will trigger simultaneously with effects triggered by the battle, but it is processed before the end of the attack. (Example: If a Digimon with <Piercing> attacks and deletes a Digimon with an [On Deletion] effect in the battle, first the [On Deletion] effect is resolved, then <Piercing> is processed.)
16-7-5. Only 1 security check can be performed during a single attack, even if <Piercing> activates multiple times. However, if the number of cards that can be checked by the attacking Digimon is modified, that number of cards will be checked in a single security check.
16-7-6. If there are no Digimon to perform a security check at the point when <Piercing> is processed, a security check won't be possible.

comprehensive-0246.title: <Fortitude>
comprehensive-0246.text:
16-27. <Fortitude>
16-27-1. <Fortitude> is a keyword effect. When a Digimon with digivolution cards and this effect is deleted, you play this Digimon without paying the cost.
16-27-2. <Fortitude> is a trigger-type effect that triggers when a Digimon with digivolution cards and this effect is deleted. (For details, refer to 15-8-3 "Trigger-Type Effects")
16-27-3. The processing from <Fortitude> is mandatory.

comprehensive-0252.title: <Vortex>
comprehensive-0252.text:
16-33. <Vortex>
16-33-1. <Vortex> allows the Digimon with this effect to attack an opponent's Digimon at the end of your turn. <Vortex> is a keyword effect that also allows a Digimon to attack in the same turn it was played.
16-33-2. <Vortex> is a trigger-type effect that triggers at the end of your turn. (For details, refer to 15-8-3 "Trigger-Type Effects")
16-33-3. The processing from <Vortex> is optional.
